source: MAFF training slide deck: "ការបញ្ជាក់គុណភាពគ្រាប់ពូជ" (Seed Quality Verification), presented by Mr. Pang Sokha, Seed Management and Development Office, 28 Nov 2014. No elibrary URL visible in the source file — this is a training presentation, not a library document.
text:
Before rice seed is graded or sold, a sample is drawn from a properly dried and cleaned seed lot and checked for several quality traits. All of the percentage tests below share the same basic shape: (weight or count of the thing you're checking for) divided by (weight or count of the whole sample), multiplied by 100.

1. Purity (ភាពសុទ្ធ): % purity = (weight of pure seed ÷ total sample weight) × 100. This tells you how much of the sample is actually the rice variety you think you're planting.

2. Other crop seed and weed/other-species seed content: same formula, but using the weight of those unwanted seeds instead of pure seed weight.

3. Inert matter / trash (កំទេចកំទីសម្រាម): % = (weight of dust, chaff, straw fragments, etc. ÷ total sample weight) × 100.

4. Mixed-variety seed (ព្រាប់ពូជលាយ): % = (weight of off-type/mixed seed ÷ total sample weight) × 100 — this catches accidental mixing with a different rice variety.

5. Red rice content (ស្រូវក្រហម): % = (weight of red rice grains ÷ total sample weight) × 100. Red rice is treated as a contaminant in certified seed lots.

6. Germination rate (អត្រាដុះ): a standard test uses three sub-samples of about 100 seeds each, placed to germinate for 5–10 days. % germination = (number of seeds that sprouted ÷ total seeds tested) × 100.

7. 1,000-seed weight: every rice variety has a published, standard weight for 1,000 seeds. To check a seed lot, weigh out 1,000 seeds from the sample and compare the result against that variety's published standard weight — a big mismatch can flag a quality or identity problem.

8. Moisture content, oven-dry method (សំណើមគ្រាប់): set an oven to 130°C. Weigh three samples of rice before drying (Mi) and place them in the oven; after 16 hours of drying, weigh them again (Mf). Moisture % = ((Mi − Mf) ÷ Mi) × 100. In the field, a calibrated moisture meter is a faster, more practical alternative to the oven method and gives comparable results for day-to-day checking.

Together, these eight checks — purity, contaminant seed content, inert matter, mixed-variety content, red rice content, germination rate, 1,000-seed weight, and moisture — are what a seed grade (Foundation/Registered/Certified/Good Seed) is actually measured against.
